logic-maze-keys.title: Maze Key Loop
logic-maze-keys.tagline: Teach a hero to pick up keys with a loop and a stop rule.
steps: Name your hero and the maze world.
Add a WHEN: story starts block.
Add a REPEAT until keys = 3 loop.
Inside the loop: MOVE forward, IF wall then TURN left, IF key then PICK UP.
After the loop: SAY 'Gate open!' and SHOW victory scene.
success: Loop runs more than once
Key count increases only when a key is found
Story ends with a clear victory line
logic-maze-keys.parent_blurb: Practices loops, conditions, and state (key count) without typing syntax. Good warm-up for Char; stretch for Vic with help on the stop rule.

story-branch-door.title: Two-Door Adventure
story-branch-door.tagline: Build a branching story where a choice changes the ending.
steps: Write a short opening scene (2–3 sentences).
Add a CHOICE block with Door A and Door B.
For Door A: calm ending with a friend.
For Door B: puzzle ending with a riddle.
Add one SAY line that only appears on the path the kid chose.
success: Two distinct endings exist
Choice is labeled clearly for a reader
No path asks for personal info
story-branch-door.parent_blurb: Classic interactive fiction. Strengthens sequencing and audience awareness. Vic's demo starts here; Char can add a third door later.

art-pixel-weather.title: Pixel Weather Painter
art-pixel-weather.tagline: Paint a sky that changes with IF sunny / IF stormy blocks.
steps: Pick a palette (warm day or cool night).
SHOW base sky scene.
Add IF weather = sunny → SHOW sun + birds.
Add IF weather = stormy → SHOW clouds + lightning flash.
Hook weather to a CHOICE so the kid can flip the scene.
success: At least two weather looks
Palette is consistent within each look
Toggle works without restarting the app
art-pixel-weather.parent_blurb: Combines visual design with conditionals. Low text load — friendly for Vic; Char can invent a third weather.

music-beat-story.title: Beat + Story Sync
music-beat-story.tagline: Layer a 4-beat loop under a short spoken story beat.
steps: Choose tempo: chill / march / bounce.
PLAY a 4-beat drum loop.
Add SAY lines timed to beat 1 and beat 3.
On beat 4: SHOW a scene change.
Stop music cleanly when the story ends.
success: Music starts before dialogue
At least two SAY lines align with beats
Music stops on END
music-beat-story.parent_blurb: Introduces timing and events. Good for Char (music + narrative); Vic can stick to one tempo.

robot-shelf-helper.title: Shelf Helper Bot
robot-shelf-helper.tagline: Simulate a bot that sorts books onto three shelves.
steps: Define shelves: Top / Middle / Bottom.
WHEN book arrives → READ label color.
IF red → MOVE to Top; IF blue → Middle; ELSE → Bottom.
SAY a short confirmation each time.
Run three books through and check the shelf map.
success: Three different books land on correct shelves
Else-path handles an unexpected color
Parent can see the shelf map on overview
robot-shelf-helper.parent_blurb: Simple robotics/sim logic: sense → decide → act. Mirrors real sorting tasks without hardware.

ai-prompt-coach.title: Kind Prompt Craft
ai-prompt-coach.tagline: Write safe story prompts that ask an AI helper for scene ideas — never personal facts.
steps: Read the Age-Safe Prompt Rules card.
Draft a prompt that asks for a fantasy setting only.
Run the local safety check (blocked words / personal asks).
Accept one scene idea into a SHOW block.
Save the prompt recipe for remixing later.
success: Prompt passes the local safety check
No real names, schools, or addresses appear
Kid can explain what the AI helper did vs what they decided
ai-prompt-coach.parent_blurb: AI literacy without open chat. Local rule checks only — no external model calls. Better fit for Char; Vic with a parent beside them.

logic-secret-code.title: Secret Code Machine
logic-secret-code.tagline: Encode a message by shifting letters, then decode it back.
steps: Pick a shift number (1–5).
WHEN encode pressed → transform each letter.
SHOW the coded message in a comic panel.
WHEN decode pressed → reverse the shift.
Verify the decoded text matches the original.
success: Encode and decode are inverses
Spaces and punctuation stay readable
Kid can explain the shift in plain words
logic-secret-code.parent_blurb: Concrete intro to algorithms and reversibility. Strong for Char; Vic can use shift=1 with a short word.

story-comic-three.title: Three-Panel Comic Code
story-comic-three.tagline: Tell a joke or mini-myth in exactly three panels controlled by blocks.
steps: Panel 1: SETUP — SHOW scene + SAY setup line.
Panel 2: TWIST — IF surprise then SHOW new prop.
Panel 3: PUNCH — SAY ending + PLAY sting sound.
Press Play Story to run panels in order.
Remix: swap the twist without breaking the order.
success: Exactly three panels run in order
Twist changes something visual
Remix still plays start → middle → end
story-comic-three.parent_blurb: Short-form narrative + sequencing. Ideal first project for Vic; Char can add a fourth 'epilogue' panel later.

art-music-festival.title: Backyard Festival Poster
art-music-festival.tagline: Design a festival poster that reacts when music starts.
steps: SHOW poster base (title + stage).
Add art layers: lights, crowd silhouettes, banner.
WHEN PLAY music → lights pulse (SHOW flash).
Add one CHOICE: day fest vs night fest palettes.
Export a parent-share blurb describing the design.
success: Poster has title + at least two layers
Music trigger changes a visual
Day/night palettes both look intentional
art-music-festival.parent_blurb: Crosses art and events. Fun showcase piece for the parent overview shelf.

robot-garden-path.title: Garden Path Rover
robot-garden-path.tagline: Program a rover to water plants along a path without leaving the garden.
steps: Draw a 3×3 garden grid with two plants.
MOVE rover to plant A, WATER, then plant B.
IF edge detected → TURN instead of leaving grid.
SAY status after each water.
Replay path twice — same route each time.
success: Both plants get watered
Rover never steps outside the grid
Replay is deterministic
robot-garden-path.parent_blurb: Spatial reasoning + safety bounds. Great for Vic; Char can add a third plant and optimize steps.

The door asks: what gets wetter the more it dries?
Beep! Hungry for a pixel biscuit.
